extraction_notes.note: Sections 6-8 are titled 'Proof of Theorem 1/2, Corollary 3'. Sections 7 and 8 are pure prose arguments and were taken as whole-section proof nodes; Section 6 is a sequence of numbered results with their own proofs, so only its opening reduction sentence (PP17) was made the proof of Theorem 1, keeping its lemmas, definitions and standing assumption as Level-1 nodes.
Remarks 1 and 2 assert results whose proofs are pointed to by PP1 ('the proofs ... are implicitly contained in Propositions'); retyped as claims so the proof can target them.
Example 2 introduces the key notion 'symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor'; kept the example and nested a definition node for that sentence.

In the proof of Proposition 5(a) the inline claim 'We show that the cyclic sum ... vanishes' is resolved only two paragraph breaks later ('we conclude that kappa is Killing'); the claim step was extended over those paragraphs instead of ending at the first break.
The proof of Lemma 16 contains a dangling citation ('The latter rules are stated in.'), and the source uses an undefined macro \undefined(m) for the unitary holonomy algebra in Section 7.

Section-overview sentences (forward announcements of what later sections show) and short commentary sentences were not made nodes; the claims inside Examples 1-3 ('the following is equivalent') stay part of the example statements.

nodes.name: Killing equation (general form)
nodes.statement: Every function is by definition Killing, i.e. the Killing condition is empty for sections of the trivial vector bundle $M\times\mathrm{I\!R}$. If $V$ is a non-trivial irreducible representation of the (special) linear group and $\gamma$ is a section of the vector bundle $VM$ associated to the frame bundle of $M$, then $\nabla \gamma$ is a section of $TM^* \otimes VM$. Decomposing the latter into irreducible subbundles according to the branching rules of Littlewood-Richardson (cf.~\cite[App.~A]{FH}), the Killing equation demands the vanishing of the Cartan component of $\nabla \gamma$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
nodes.statement_short: A section of an associated bundle is Killing iff the Cartan component of its covariant derivative vanishes; every function is Killing.

nodes.name: Existence of the prolongation of the Killing equation
nodes.statement: Because the Killing equation is of finite type, the existence and uniqueness of the prolongation of the Killing equation is a priori ensured from an abstract point of view (cf.~\cite{BCEG}). Thus there exists a vector bundle $\mathrm{Prol}(VM) \to M$ equipped with a linear connection and a linear assignment $\Gamma(VM)\to \Gamma(\mathrm{Prol}(VM))$ such that Killing tensors correspond with parallel sections of $\mathrm{Prol}(VM)$.
nodes.section: 1 Introduction
assumptions: the Killing equation is of finite type
conclusions: there exists a vector bundle $\mathrm{Prol}(VM) \to M$ equipped with a linear connection and a linear assignment $\Gamma(VM)\to \Gamma(\mathrm{Prol}(VM))$ such that Killing tensors correspond with parallel sections of $\mathrm{Prol}(VM)$
nodes.statement_short: Killing tensors correspond to parallel sections of a prolongation bundle with a linear connection.

nodes.name: Killing equation for p-forms
nodes.statement: For example, the Killing equation for $p$-forms is $\mathrm{d}\omega = (p+1) \nabla\omega$ for all $p\geq 0$, where $\mathrm{d}$ and $\nabla$ denote the exterior differential and the Levi-Civita connection.
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms

nodes.name: Special Killing form
nodes.statement: A Killing form $\omega$ is called special if it satisfies $\nabla_X \mathrm{d} \omega = - c\, X^\sharp\wedge \omega$ for some constant $c > 0$, where $X^\sharp$ denotes the dual of a vector field $X$ (cf.~\cite[Chapter~3]{Se}).
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms

nodes.name: Cone over M and associated (p+1)-form
nodes.statement: To every pair $(\omega,\eta)$ of a $p$-form $\omega$ and a $p+1$-form $\eta$ on $M$ we associate the $p+1$-form $r^p \mathrm{d} r \wedge \omega + \frac{r^{p+1}}{p+1} \eta$ on the cone $\hat M := M\times \mathrm{I\!R}_+$ (cf.~\cite[3.2.4]{Se}).
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms
nodes.statement_short: Associates to a p-form and a (p+1)-form a (p+1)-form on the cone $\hat M = M\times\mathbb{R}_+$.

nodes.name: Special Killing forms correspond to parallel forms on the cone
nodes.statement: Then it is easy to see that $\omega$ is a special Killing form if and only if the $p+1$-form $\hat\omega := \frac{1}{p+1} \mathrm{d} ( r^{p+1} \omega)$ associated with the pair $(\omega,\mathrm{d} \omega)$ is Levi-Civita parallel with respect to the cone metric. On the other hand, a parallel $p+1$-form on the cone yields a special Killing $p$-form on $M$ by inserting the radial vector field at $r=1$. Thus there is a 1-1 correspondence between parallel $p+1$-forms on the cone and special Killing $p$-forms on $M$.
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms
conclusions: $\omega$ is a special Killing form if and only if the $p+1$-form $\hat\omega := \frac{1}{p+1} \mathrm{d} ( r^{p+1} \omega)$ associated with the pair $(\omega,\mathrm{d} \omega)$ is Levi-Civita parallel with respect to the cone metric
there is a 1-1 correspondence between parallel $p+1$-forms on the cone and special Killing $p$-forms on $M$
nodes.statement_short: Special Killing p-forms on M are in 1-1 correspondence with parallel (p+1)-forms on the metric cone.

nodes.name: Gallot's characterization of the sphere by equation (E_1)
nodes.statement: Moreover, specifying $p = 0$, i.e. $\omega$ is a function $f$, we recover that a non-vanishing function $f$ satisfying the second order differential equation $\nabla^2 f = n\cdot g\cdot f$ (denoted by $(E_1)$ in~\cite{Ga}) exists only on the unit-sphere.
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms
assumptions: a non-vanishing function $f$ satisfying the second order differential equation $\nabla^2 f = n\cdot g\cdot f$
conclusions: exists only on the unit-sphere
nodes.statement_short: A non-vanishing solution of $\nabla^2 f = n g f$ exists only on the unit sphere (Gallot's (E_1)).

nodes.name: Prolongation of the Killing equation for forms
nodes.statement: Every Killing $p$-form $\omega$ also satisfies the second order equation $\nabla_X\mathrm{d}\, \omega = \frac{p+1}{p}R^+(X)\omega$, the prolongation of the Killing equation. Here $R^+(X)$ denotes the natural action of degree one of the endomorphism valued 1-form $R_{X,\bullet}$ on forms (cf.~\cite[Chapter~4]{Se}).
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms
conclusions: also satisfies the second order equation $\nabla_X\mathrm{d}\, \omega = \frac{p+1}{p}R^+(X)\omega$

nodes.name: Killing forms are parallel sections for the Killing connection
nodes.statement: In particular, a form $\omega$ is Killing if and only if the prolongation $(\omega,\mathrm{d} \omega)$ is parallel with respect to a natural linear connection on the corresponding vector bundle, the Killing connection.
nodes.section: 1.1 Killing forms
conclusions: a form $\omega$ is Killing if and only if the prolongation $(\omega,\mathrm{d} \omega)$ is parallel with respect to a natural linear connection on the corresponding vector bundle, the Killing connection
equivalent_conditions: the prolongation $(\omega,\mathrm{d} \omega)$ is parallel with respect to a natural linear connection on the corresponding vector bundle

nodes.name: Special Killing forms via the prolonged equation on the sphere
nodes.statement: Moreover, on the unit sphere we have $R^+(X)\omega = - p\,X^*\wedge \omega$. In other words, a Killing form is special if and only if the prolonged Killing equation has the same form as generally for Killing forms on a round sphere.

nodes.name: Symmetric Killing 2-tensor
nodes.statement: A symmetric 2-tensor $\kappa$ is Killing if the completely symmetric part of $\nabla\kappa$ vanishes, i.e. \begin{equation} \forall p\in M,x\in T_pM:\;\nabla_x\kappa(x,x)\;\;=\;\;0. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Variables of the prolongation for symmetric 2-tensors
nodes.statement: Quite differently, for symmetric 2-tensors the variables of the prolongation are triples $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)\in \mathbb{S}_{T_0}V^*\oplus \mathbb{S}_{T_1}V^*\oplus\mathbb{S}_{T_2}V^*$ of tensors of different symmetry types described by Young tableaus $T_i$ of shapes $(2,i)$ for $i =0,1,2$, see~\eqref{eq:kappa_prolong_1}-\eqref{eq:kappa_prolong_2} and~\eqref{eq:def_C_kappa}-\eqref{eq:def_S_kappa} below.
nodes.section: 1.2 A brief overview on our results for symmetric tensors
nodes.statement_short: For symmetric 2-tensors the prolongation variables are triples of tensors of Young symmetry types (2,0), (2,1), (2,2).

nodes.name: Explicit Killing prolongation for all symmetry types
nodes.statement: Although their arguments can not immediately be generalised to other symmetry types, nevertheless one would conjecture that similar explicit constructions are possible for all symmetry types of tensors.

nodes.statement: Further, as a consequence of the branching rules due to Littlewood-Richardson, it is immediately clear that $\mathbb{S}^\star_TV^*$ is a subspace of the kernel of the bilinear map \begin{align} &\ell_{ij}^\star \colon \Lambda^{\mu_i}V^*\times \Lambda^{\mu_j}V^*\to \Lambda^{\mu_i+1}V^*\otimes \Lambda^{\mu_j-1}V^*,\quad (\omega_i,\omega_j) \mapsto \ell_{ij}^\star(\omega_i,\omega_j):\\ & \ell_{ij}^\star(\omega_i,\omega_j)(v_1,\ldots,v_{\mu_i+\mu_j})\;\;:=\;\; \sum_{a=1}^{\mu_i+1}(-1)^{a+\mu_i+1}\omega_i(v_1,\cdots,\hat v_a,\ldots,v_{\mu_i+1})\omega_j(v_a,v_{\mu_i+2},\ldots,v_{\mu_i+\mu_j}), \end{align} which anti-symmetrizes all the indizes of $\omega_i$ with one further index of $\omega_j$ for $i<j$. Moreover, it is also easy to see that $\mathbb{S}^\star_TV^*$ is in fact equal to the intersection of the Kernels of all $\ell_{ij}^\star$ taken over all $1\leq i < j \leq \ell$.

nodes.name: Curvature-type tableau and the first Bianchi identity
nodes.statement: Consider the tableau $T := \scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 2 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{16pt}$. The tensor products $\Lambda^2V^*\otimes \Lambda^2V^*$ and $\Lambda^3V^*\otimes V^*$ decompose according to the Littlewood-Richardson rules as follows \begin{align*} \Lambda^2V^*\otimes \Lambda^2V^* & = \Lambda^4V^*\oplus \mathbb{S}^\star_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 3\\ \cline{1-2} 2 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{} \\ \cline{1-1} 4 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{}\\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}} V^*\oplus \mathbb{S}^\star_TV^*,\\ \Lambda^3V^*\otimes V^* &= \Lambda^4V^*\oplus \mathbb{S}^\star_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 3\\ \cline{1-2} 2 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{} \\ \cline{1-1} 4 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{}\\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}} V^*. \end{align*} The first two factors are already skew-symmetric in the first three indices and hence $\ell_{12}^\star$ yields isomorphisms between the first and second summands in each decomposition, respectively. Therefore, it necessarily vanishes on $\mathbb{S}^\star_TV^*$. From this we see that $\mathbb{S}^\star_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 2 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}V^*$ describes the subspace of $\Lambda^2V^*\otimes \Lambda^2V^*$ given by those tensors which satisfy the first Bianchi identity, i.e algebraic prototypes of the curvature tensor $\tilde R(x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)$ of some Riemannian manifold $\tilde M$ at some point $p\in \tilde M$ (cf. also~\cite[p.12]{Sch}). The only exchange rule of order two leads to pair symmetry, which is a well known algebraic consequence of the first Bianchi identity in $\Lambda^2V^*\otimes \Lambda^2V^*$.

nodes.statement_short: The (2,2) tableau with columns {1,2},{3,4} describes tensors satisfying the first Bianchi identity.

nodes.name: Trivial solutions from the metric tensor
nodes.statement: We would like to remark that there are always trivial solutions to~(a),~(b) and~(c) of the previous theorem coming from the metric tensor. For example a constant multiple $\kappa := c\, g$ of the metric tensor is in accordance with~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1},~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2}. Further, it is easy to see that the requirement that the dimension of $M$ has to be strictly larger than one is necessary, see Remark~\ref{re:main_3}.

nodes.name: Spaces of constant curvature
nodes.statement: If $M$ is simply connected and of constant (non-vanishing) sectional curvature, then we can realise $M$ as a standard model in the pseudo Euclidean space $(V^{n+1},\langle\ ,\ \rangle)$. Further, possibly after reversing the sign of the metric of $M$ and scaling by a positive constant, we can assume that $M$ is the generalised unit sphere $\{v\in V|\langle v,v\rangle = 1\}$. Then the cone over $M$ is $V\setminus\{0\}$ and the nullity conditions~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} become tautological. Thus algebraic curvature tensors on $V$ correspond with elements of $\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}V^*$ via~\eqref{eq:symmetrized_curvature_tensor}. We obtain from $(a)\Leftrightarrow (c)$ that symmetric Killing 2-tensors on $M$ are in 1-1 correspondence with algebraic curvature tensors on $V$ (the flat case is handeled similarly). Thus we have recovered the main result of~\cite{McMS} in the special case of 2-tensors.
nodes.section: 3 The main results
nodes.statement_short: On a generalised unit sphere the cone is flat, so Killing 2-tensors correspond to algebraic curvature tensors on $V$ (McLenaghan-Milson-Smirnov).

nodes.name: Classification of complete simply connected manifolds admitting parallel curvature tensors on the cone
nodes.statement: The classification of complete and simply connected Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$ with respect to Theorem~\ref{th:main_1} is as follows. \begin{itemize} \item On a round sphere the space of symmetric Killing 2-tensors is isomorphic to the linear space of algebraic curvature tensors in dimension $n+1$, see Example~\ref{ex:constant_curvature}. \item Suppose that $(M,g)$ is a 3-Sasakian manifold which is not of constant sectional curvature. Let $\{\eta_1,\eta_2,\eta_3\}$ denote its characteristic forms related to Kähler forms $\{\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3\}$ on the cone. Here the symmetrized tensor products $\eta_i\bullet\eta_j$ are symmetric Killing 2-tensors which correspond to the parallel symmetrized algebraic curvature tensors $\omega_i\owedge\omega_j$ on the cone. The pair $(\kappa,C^\kappa)$ with $\kappa := \eta_i\bullet\eta_j$ and $C^\kappa := \frac{1}{4} \mathrm{d}\eta_i\owedge\mathrm{d}\eta_j$ is a solution to~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1}-\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_2}. Together with the metric tensor we obtain a 7-dimensional space of symmetric 2-tensors matching for example~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1},\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} of Theorem~\ref{th:main_1}~a). \item Suppose that $(M,g)$ is a Sasakian manifold which is neither 3-Sasakian nor of constant sectional curvature one. Let $\eta$ denote its characteristic 1-form. Similar as in the 3-Sasakian case, the set of Killing tensors fitting into Theorem~\ref{th:main_1} is the 2-dimensional space spanned by the square $\eta \otimes \eta $ of the characteristic form and the metric tensor. \item Otherwise, there are only the obvious solutions to (a),~(b) or~(c) coming from the metric tensor. \end{itemize}

assumptions: complete and simply connected Riemannian manifolds $(M,g)$

nodes.name: Argument for Corollary 2
nodes.statement: Due to the fact that a Sasakian vector field has constant length, the square of the characteristic form of a Sasakian manifold has constant trace. The same is true for the symmetric products of the characteristic forms of a 3-Sasakian manifold. Conversely, the Killing tensor $\kappa$ associated with a parallel curvature tensor $S$ of $\mathrm{I\!R}^{n+1}$ on an $n$-dimensional round sphere has $\mathrm{d}\, \mathrm{tr} \kappa \neq 0$ unless the algebraic Ricci-tensor of $S$ is a multiple of the Euclidean scalar product (i.e. unless $S$ has the algebraic properties of the curvature tensor of an Einstein manifold). Therefore:

nodes.statement_short: Sasakian and 3-Sasakian Killing tensors have constant trace, while sphere Killing tensors from non-Einstein curvature tensors do not.

nodes.name: Reduction of the frame bundle of the cone
nodes.statement: Every basis of $T_pM$ can be extended to a basis of $T_{(p,r)}\hat M$ using the radial vector $\partial_r|_{(p,r)}$. Thus, the principal $\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(\mathrm{I\!R})$ fiber bundle of frames of the vector bundle $T\hat M$ admits a natural reduction to the principal $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathrm{I\!R})$ fiber bundle of frames of the pullback vector bundle $\tau^*TM$. In particular, $\nabla$ induces a connection on every tensor bundle of $T\hat M$. nodes.name: Branching rules for symmetrized curvature tensors on the cone
nodes.statement: The vector bundle $\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*\hat M$ admits a decomposition into three direct summands \begin{equation} \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{6pt}}\,T^*M\oplus \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 2 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 1 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{\;\;\;} \\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}}\,T^*M \oplus \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*M \end{equation} which is parallel with respect to the Levi-Civita connection of $M$. Suitable projection maps are given as follows: \begin{eqnarray} \mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*\hat M\to \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{6pt}}\,T^*M, & & S \mapsto \alpha^S \;\;:= \;\; \frac{1}{2}\partial_r\lrcorner \partial_r \lrcorner S\;,\\ \mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*\hat M\to \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 2 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 1 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{\;\;\;}\\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}}T^*M \;,& & S \mapsto \beta^S \;\;:= \;\; \iota^* \partial_r \lrcorner S\;,\\ \mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*\hat M \to \tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4\\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}T^*M \;,& & S\mapsto \gamma^S \;\;:= \;\; \iota^*S. \end{eqnarray} Then every triple $(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ defines the symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor \begin{equation} S := \alpha \owedge\mathrm{d} r \bullet \mathrm{d} r + \beta \owedge\mathrm{d} r + \gamma. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
nodes.statement: It is straightforward to verify~\eqref{eq:S_explizit}. Hence the map which projects from $\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, T^*\hat M $ to $\tau^*\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{6pt}}\,T^*M \oplus\mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 2 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 1 & \multicolumn{1}{c}{\;\;\;} \\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}}\,T^*M \oplus \mathbb{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\,T^ *M $ along $\tau$ is surjective. In order to demonstrate its injectivity, suppose $\alpha^S = 0$, $\beta^S = 0$ and $\gamma^S = 0$. Then $S(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4)$ vanishes whenever at least two of the vectors $u_i$ are horizontal by means of the symmetries of a curvature tensor. On the other hand, if at most one vector is horizontal, then at least three are proportional to $\partial_r$ and thus $S(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4) = 0$, since $S$ satisfies the corresponding exchange rule of order one between rows. nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: We have $\hat \nabla_xS - \nabla_xS = x\lrcorner \Delta\cdot S$, where $\Delta$ is defined by~\eqref{eq:Delta} and $\cdot$ is the usual action of endomorphisms on tensors by algebraic derivation, see~\eqref{eq:derivation}. Hence, \begin{align*} x\lrcorner \Delta S(\partial_r,\partial_r,y_1,y_2) &\;\;=\;\; \frac{- 2}{r}\underbrace{\langle \partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p \rangle}_{=1} S( \partial_r,x,y_1,y_2). \end{align*} This yields the first component in~\eqref{eq:second_fundamental_form_of_bbP}. For the second, we use that the cyclic sum of $y\lrcorner S$ vanishes for fixed $y$. Hence $ 2\, S(x,z,y,z) = 2\, S(y,z,x,z) = - S(y,x,z,z) = - S(z,z,x,y)$. We get \begin{align*} & x\lrcorner \Delta S(\partial_r,y_1,y_2,y_3) &\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace\begin{array}{cc}- \frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_1 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3)\\ + r\, \langle x,y_2 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p) \end{array} \right \rbrace\\ & &\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace\begin{array}{cc}-\frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_1 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3)\\ - \frac{1}{2} r\, \langle x,y_2 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_3) & - \frac{1}{2}r\, \langle x,y_3 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2) \end{array} \right \rbrace\\ & &\;\;=\;\;& - \frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) + r\, \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 2 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 1 \\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, \langle x, y_1\rangle \alpha(y_2,y_3)\\ & & \;\;\stackrel{\eqref{eq:product_of_a_one_form_and_a_symmetric_2-tensor}}{=}\;\; & - \frac{1}{r} \gamma(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) + 2\,r\, \alpha\owedge x^\sharp (y_1,y_2,y_3) \end{align*} for all $x,y_1,\ldots,y_3\in T_pM$. For the last component: on the one side, we have \begin{align*} x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace \begin{array}{c}\ \;r\, \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) + r\, \langle x,y_2\rangle S(y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_3,y_4)\\ + r\, \langle x,y_3\rangle S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4) + r\, \langle x,y_4\rangle S(y_1,y_2,y_3,\partial_r|_p)\end{array}\right \rbrace\\ \end{align*} for all $x,y_1,\ldots,y_4\in T_pM$. On the other side, \begin{align*} 3\, \beta \owedge x^\sharp (x,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;\stackrel{\eqref{eq:noch_ein_produkt}}{=}\;\; & \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, \langle x, y_1 \rangle \beta (y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ \;\;=\;\; & \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ - \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_1,y_4)\\ - \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_3,y_2)\\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_1,y_2)\end{array}\right ). \end{align*} The first and the last line of the above term yield \begin{equation*} \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_1,y_2)\end{array}\right ) \;\;=\;\; \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4)\end{array}\right )\\ \end{equation*} which gives $\frac{2}{r} x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)$. The two lines in the middle are by the Bianchi identity \begin{align*} - \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_1,y_4)\\ + \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_3,y_2) \end{array}\right ) &\;\;=\;\;& \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3 \rangle\big ( S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4) + S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2,y_4)\big )\\ + \langle x,y_1\rangle \big (S(y_3,y_4,\partial_r|_p,y_2) + S(\partial_r|_p,y_3,y_4,y_2)\big ) \end{array}\right ). \end{align*} Using the Bianchi identity in the form mentioned further above, this yields \begin{align*} \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3 \rangle\big ( S(y_2,y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_4) - \frac{1}{2}S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4)\big )\\ \langle x,y_1\rangle \big (S(y_4,y_3,\partial_r|_p,y_2) - \frac{1}{2} S(y_3,y_4,\partial_r|_p,y_2)\big ) \end{array}\right ), \end{align*} which adds $\frac{1}{r}x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)$ to the Young symmetrizer. We conclude that \begin{align*} \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\,\langle x, y_1 \rangle \partial_r\lrcorner S(y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;=\;\;\frac{3}{r}x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4). \end{align*} This yields the last component of~\eqref{eq:second_fundamental_form_of_bbP}.
nodes.section: 4.1 Symmetric Killing 2-tensors whose associated symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor is parallel
nodes.statement_short: Compute $x\lrcorner\Delta\cdot S$ component by component, using Bianchi-type identities for the last component.

nodes.name: First component

nodes.name: Second component
nodes.statement: For the second, we use that the cyclic sum of $y\lrcorner S$ vanishes for fixed $y$. Hence $ 2\, S(x,z,y,z) = 2\, S(y,z,x,z) = - S(y,x,z,z) = - S(z,z,x,y)$. We get \begin{align*} & x\lrcorner \Delta S(\partial_r,y_1,y_2,y_3) &\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace\begin{array}{cc}- \frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_1 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3)\\ + r\, \langle x,y_2 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p) \end{array} \right \rbrace\\ & &\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace\begin{array}{cc}-\frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) & + r\, \langle x,y_1 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3)\\ - \frac{1}{2} r\, \langle x,y_2 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_3) & - \frac{1}{2}r\, \langle x,y_3 \rangle S(\partial_r|_p,\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2) \end{array} \right \rbrace\\ & &\;\;=\;\;& - \frac{1}{r} S(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) + r\, \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 2 & 3 \\ \cline{1-2} 1 \\ \cline{1-1} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, \langle x, y_1\rangle \alpha(y_2,y_3)\\ & & \;\;\stackrel{\eqref{eq:product_of_a_one_form_and_a_symmetric_2-tensor}}{=}\;\; & - \frac{1}{r} \gamma(x,y_1,y_2,y_3) + 2\,r\, \alpha\owedge x^\sharp (y_1,y_2,y_3) \end{align*} for all $x,y_1,\ldots,y_3\in T_pM$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Symmetric Killing 2-tensors whose associated symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor is parallel
nodes.statement_short: Use the Bianchi identity to compute the second component.

nodes.name: Last component: two expressions
nodes.statement: For the last component: on the one side, we have \begin{align*} x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;=\;\;& \left \lbrace \begin{array}{c}\ \;r\, \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) + r\, \langle x,y_2\rangle S(y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_3,y_4)\\ + r\, \langle x,y_3\rangle S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4) + r\, \langle x,y_4\rangle S(y_1,y_2,y_3,\partial_r|_p)\end{array}\right \rbrace\\ \end{align*} for all $x,y_1,\ldots,y_4\in T_pM$. On the other side, \begin{align*} 3\, \beta \owedge x^\sharp (x,y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;\stackrel{\eqref{eq:noch_ein_produkt}}{=}\;\; & \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\, \langle x, y_1 \rangle \beta (y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ \;\;=\;\; & \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ - \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_1,y_4)\\ - \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_3,y_2)\\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_1,y_2)\end{array}\right ). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 4.1 Symmetric Killing 2-tensors whose associated symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor is parallel
nodes.statement_short: Write the last component and the Young-symmetrized product with $\beta$.

nodes.name: Outer lines
nodes.statement: The first and the last line of the above term yield \begin{equation*} \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_1,y_2)\end{array}\right ) \;\;=\;\; \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34}\left ( \begin{array}{c}\langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_3,y_4) \\ + \langle x,y_3\rangle S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4)\end{array}\right )\\ \end{equation*} which gives $\frac{2}{r} x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)$.
nodes.section: 4.1 Symmetric Killing 2-tensors whose associated symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor is parallel
nodes.statement_short: The outer lines give $\frac{2}{r}x\lrcorner\Delta S$.

nodes.name: Middle lines via Bianchi
nodes.statement: The two lines in the middle are by the Bianchi identity \begin{align*} - \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_2,y_1,y_4)\\ + \langle x,y_1\rangle S(\partial_r|_p,y_4,y_3,y_2) \end{array}\right ) &\;\;=\;\;& \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3 \rangle\big ( S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4) + S(\partial_r|_p,y_1,y_2,y_4)\big )\\ + \langle x,y_1\rangle \big (S(y_3,y_4,\partial_r|_p,y_2) + S(\partial_r|_p,y_3,y_4,y_2)\big ) \end{array}\right ). \end{align*} Using the Bianchi identity in the form mentioned further above, this yields \begin{align*} \mathfrak{S}_{12}\mathfrak{S}_{34} \left ( \begin{array}{c} \langle x,y_3 \rangle\big ( S(y_2,y_1,\partial_r|_p,y_4) - \frac{1}{2}S(y_1,y_2,\partial_r|_p,y_4)\big )\\ \langle x,y_1\rangle \big (S(y_4,y_3,\partial_r|_p,y_2) - \frac{1}{2} S(y_3,y_4,\partial_r|_p,y_2)\big ) \end{array}\right ), \end{align*} which adds $\frac{1}{r}x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4)$ to the Young symmetrizer.
nodes.section: 4.1 Symmetric Killing 2-tensors whose associated symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor is parallel
nodes.statement_short: Bianchi identity turns the middle lines into $\frac{1}{r}x\lrcorner\Delta S$.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: We conclude that \begin{align*} \mathrm{S}_{\scaleto{\begin{array}{|c|c|} \cline{1-2} 1 & 2 \\ \cline{1-2} 3 & 4 \\ \cline{1-2} \end{array}}{12pt}}\,\langle x, y_1 \rangle \partial_r\lrcorner S(y_2,y_3,y_4)\;\;=\;\;\frac{3}{r}x\lrcorner \Delta S(y_1,y_2,y_3,y_4). \end{align*} This yields the last component of~\eqref{eq:second_fundamental_form_of_bbP}.

Let $S$ be a symmetrized algebraic curvature tensor on the cone seen as a triple $(\alpha, eta,\gamma)$ according to~\eqref{eq:glndec}. The following assertions (a) - (d) are equivalent:  egin{enumerate} \item $\hat
abla S = 0$. \item The pair $(\kappa,C)\;:=\;(\alpha|_M,\gamma|_M)$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1}-\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_2}, $

For $(a) \Rightarrow (b)$: since $\hat 
abla S^\kappa = 0$, the curvature endomorphism $\hat R_{x,y}$ annihilates $S$ for all $p\in M$ and $x,y\in T_pM$. Because $\hat R$ is horizontal, we conclude that $\hat R$ annihilates the components of~\eqref{eq:zerlegung_von_kappa_dach}. In particular, $\hat R_{x,y}\cdot \kappa = 0$ and $\hat R_{x,y} \cdot 
abla\kappa = 0$ for all $p\in M$ and $x,y\in T_pM$. Using~\eqref{eq:hat_R_1}, we see that both~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} hold. For $(b)\Rightarrow (a)$: by assumption,~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} hold. The expression $F^1(\kappa,R)$ is explicitly described in~\eqref{eq:def_F21}. From this one sees that it depends in fact only on the action $R_{x,y}\cdot \kappa$ of the given algebraic curvature tensor $R$ on $\kappa$. Therefore~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} implies that $F^1(R,\kappa) = F^1(R_1,\kappa)$. Similarly, the explicit description~\eqref{eq:def_F22} of $F^2(\kappa,R)$ implies that the latter expression depends only on the actions $R_{x,y}\cdot\kappa$ and $R_{x,y}\cdot 
abla \kappa$ of the algebraic curvature tensor $R$ on $\kappa$ and $
abla\kappa$. We obtain from~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} that $F^2(\kappa,R) = F^2(\kappa,R_1)$. Then we conclude from Lemma~ef{le:curvature_terms_for_S1} that $F^1(\kappa,R)$ and $F^2(\kappa,R)$ are given by~\eqref{eq:F21_speziell} and~\eqref{eq:F22_speziell}. nodes.name: (a) implies (b)
nodes.statement: For $(a) \Rightarrow (b)$: since $\hat \nabla S^\kappa = 0$, the curvature endomorphism $\hat R_{x,y}$ annihilates $S$ for all $p\in M$ and $x,y\in T_pM$. Because $\hat R$ is horizontal, we conclude that $\hat R$ annihilates the components of~\eqref{eq:zerlegung_von_kappa_dach}. In particular, $\hat R_{x,y}\cdot \kappa = 0$ and $\hat R_{x,y} \cdot \nabla\kappa = 0$ for all $p\in M$ and $x,y\in T_pM$. Using~\eqref{eq:hat_R_1}, we see that both~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} hold.
nodes.section: 5.3 Prolongation of symmetric Killing 2-tensors in spaces of constant curvature

nodes.name: (b) implies (a)
nodes.statement: For $(b)\Rightarrow (a)$: by assumption,~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} hold. The expression $F^1(\kappa,R)$ is explicitly described in~\eqref{eq:def_F21}. From this one sees that it depends in fact only on the action $R_{x,y}\cdot \kappa$ of the given algebraic curvature tensor $R$ on $\kappa$. Therefore~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} implies that $F^1(R,\kappa) = F^1(R_1,\kappa)$. Similarly, the explicit description~\eqref{eq:def_F22} of $F^2(\kappa,R)$ implies that the latter expression depends only on the actions $R_{x,y}\cdot\kappa$ and $R_{x,y}\cdot \nabla \kappa$ of the algebraic curvature tensor $R$ on $\kappa$ and $\nabla\kappa$. We obtain from~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_1} and~\eqref{eq:curv_cond_2} that $F^2(\kappa,R) = F^2(\kappa,R_1)$. Hence the result follows from Proposition~\ref{p:prolong}.

abla^2_{y,x}\kappa =

abla^2_{x,x}\kappa(x,y) \end{align*} for all $x\in T_pM_1$ and $y\in T_qM_2$. Hence, the exchange rule $C(x,x,x,y) = 0$ implies from~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1} that  egin{align*} 0 \;\;=\;\; - \langle x, xangle \kappa (x,y) + \underbrace{\langle x, yangle \kappa (x,x)}_{=0} \end{align*} We conclude that $ \kappa (x,y) = 0$, i.e. $\kappa = \kappa_1 + \kappa_2$ where $\kappa_1$ and $\kappa_2$ are the restrictions of $\kappa$ to $T_pM_1	imes T_pM_1$ and $T_qM_2	imes T_qM_2$, respectively. Further, the symmetry $C(x,y,x,y) = C(y,x,x,y)$ and the commuting of the covariant derivatives $
abla^2_{x,y}\kappa(x,y) = 
abla^2_{y,x}\kappa(x,y)$ yields  egin{equation*} \langle x, xangle \kappa (y,y)\;\;=\;\;\langle y, yangle \kappa (x,x) \end{equation*} Hence $\kappa(x,x) = \kappa(y,y)$ for all unit vectors $x\in T_pM_1$ and $y\in T_qM_2$. Thus there exists a function $f \colon M_1	imes M_2 	o \mathrm{I\!R}_+$ such that $\kappa_1(x,x) = f(p,q) = \kappa_2(y,y)$ for all unit vectors $x$ and $y$, i.e. $\kappa = f\langle\ ,\ angle$. Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bianchis_cyclic_sum_is_parallel} implies that $(n + 2)\mathrm{d} f$ is parallel, hence $
abla \mathrm{d} f = 0$. nodes.statement: Hence, the exchange rule $C(x,x,x,y) = 0$ implies from~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1} that \begin{align*} 0 \;\;=\;\; - \langle x, x\rangle \kappa (x,y) + \underbrace{\langle x, y\rangle \kappa (x,x)}_{=0} \end{align*} We conclude that $ \kappa (x,y) = 0$, i.e. $\kappa = \kappa_1 + \kappa_2$ where $\kappa_1$ and $\kappa_2$ are the restrictions of $\kappa$ to $T_pM_1\times T_pM_1$ and $T_qM_2\times T_qM_2$, respectively.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: The exchange rule forces $\kappa(x,y)=0$, so $\kappa$ splits.

nodes.name: kappa is conformal to g
nodes.statement: Further, the symmetry $C(x,y,x,y) = C(y,x,x,y)$ and the commuting of the covariant derivatives $\nabla^2_{x,y}\kappa(x,y) = \nabla^2_{y,x}\kappa(x,y)$ yields \begin{equation*} \langle x, x\rangle \kappa (y,y)\;\;=\;\;\langle y, y\rangle \kappa (x,x) \end{equation*} Hence $\kappa(x,x) = \kappa(y,y)$ for all unit vectors $x\in T_pM_1$ and $y\in T_qM_2$. Thus there exists a function $f \colon M_1\times M_2 \to \mathrm{I\!R}_+$ such that $\kappa_1(x,x) = f(p,q) = \kappa_2(y,y)$ for all unit vectors $x$ and $y$, i.e. $\kappa = f\langle\ ,\ \rangle$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Symmetries give $\kappa = f g$.

nodes.name: df vanishes
nodes.statement: Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bianchis_cyclic_sum_is_parallel} implies that $(n + 2)\mathrm{d} f$ is parallel, hence $\nabla \mathrm{d} f = 0$. Substituting this into~\eqref{eq:erste_vorstufe_zur_Bianchi_identity} yields \begin{align*} & \mathfrak{S}_{123}\, \mathrm{d}_{x_1}f \langle x_2,x_3 \rangle\;\;=\;\;3\,n\, \langle x_2,x_3\rangle \mathrm{d}_{x_1}f + (n-1) \mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle\, \mathrm{d}_{x_3}f. \end{align*} Evaluating this equation with $x_1 = x_2 = x_3$ implies that $(n - 1) \mathrm{d} f = 0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Inserting into Lemmas 9 and 12 forces $(n-1)\mathrm{d}f = 0$.

nodes.name: Conclusion
nodes.statement: Therefore if $n > 1$ then $\kappa$ is a constant multiple of the metric tensor. We conclude that $M$ is irreducible.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: $\kappa$ is a constant multiple of $g$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Contracted Killing equation
nodes.statement: If $\dim(M) \geq 2$, then the contraction~\eqref{eq:divergenz_versus_differential_der_spur} of the Killing equation holds.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
conclusions: the contraction~\eqref{eq:divergenz_versus_differential_der_spur} of the Killing equation holds
nodes.label: co:contracted_Bianchi_identity

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 5
nodes.statement: We can assume that $\kappa$ is not a constant multiple of the metric tensor, since otherwise~\eqref{eq:divergenz_versus_differential_der_spur} is obvious. Then, on the one hand, $M$ is irreducible by the previous lemma and hence the holonomy group acts fixed point free on tangent vectors, because $\dim(M)\geq 2$. On the other hand, since the contraction of~\eqref{eq:Bianchis_cyclic_sum_is_parallel} implies that the 1-form $\lambda\;:=\;\mathrm{d} \, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa - 2 \delta \kappa$ is parallel, the latter is fixed under the holonomy group at each point. We conclude that $\lambda = 0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: The parallel 1-form $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa - 2\delta\kappa$ is holonomy-fixed on an irreducible manifold, hence zero.

nodes.name: Reduce to non-trivial kappa
nodes.statement: We can assume that $\kappa$ is not a constant multiple of the metric tensor, since otherwise~\eqref{eq:divergenz_versus_differential_der_spur} is obvious.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: WLOG $\kappa$ is not a multiple of $g$.

nodes.name: Irreducibility
nodes.statement: Then, on the one hand, $M$ is irreducible by the previous lemma and hence the holonomy group acts fixed point free on tangent vectors, because $\dim(M)\geq 2$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 13 the holonomy acts without fixed vectors.

nodes.name: Parallel 1-form vanishes
nodes.statement: On the other hand, since the contraction of~\eqref{eq:Bianchis_cyclic_sum_is_parallel} implies that the 1-form $\lambda\;:=\;\mathrm{d} \, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa - 2 \delta \kappa$ is parallel, the latter is fixed under the holonomy group at each point. We conclude that $\lambda = 0$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: $\lambda = \mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa - 2\delta\kappa$ is parallel, hence zero.

nodes.name: Equation (83)
nodes.statement: 2 \mathfrak{S}_{123} \nabla_{y_2} \kappa (y_1,y_3) &\;\;=\;\;\left \lbrace \begin{array}{c} 3\nabla^3_{y_1,y_2,y_3}\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa + 6\, \mathrm{d} \, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa(y_1) \langle y_2,y_3\rangle + 3\,\mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle\, \mathrm{d} \, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa(y_3) \end{array} \right \rbrace,

nodes.label: eq:vergleich_der_spur_von_kappa_mit_der_skalaren_kruemmung_von_C

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary 6
nodes.statement: This follows by substituting~\eqref{eq:divergenz_versus_differential_der_spur} into~\eqref{eq:erste_vorstufe_zur_Bianchi_identity} and~\eqref{eq:differential_der_skalaren_spur_von_C}, respectively.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Substitute Corollary 5 into Lemmas 12 and 11.

nodes.name: Constant curvature tensor R_1
nodes.statement: Let $R_1$ denote the algebraic curvature tensor defined by \begin{equation} R_1(x,y,z)\;:=\;- \langle x , z \rangle y + \langle y , z \rangle x \end{equation} for all $x,y,z\in T_pM$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
also_stated_at: This enables us to calculate $F^1(\kappa,R_1)$ and $F^2(\kappa,R_1)$ with $R_1(x,y)\;:=\;- x\wedge y$ on every pseudo Riemannian manifold $M$ as follows.

nodes.statement: R_1(x,y,z)\;:=\;- \langle x , z \rangle y + \langle y , z \rangle x
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1

nodes.name: 1-nullity
nodes.statement: Recall that the $1$-nullity of a pseudo Riemannian manifold is the subspace of $T_pM$ defined by \begin{equation} \mathcal{C}_1(T_pM)\;:=\;\{x\in T_pM| R(x,y,z)= R_1(x,y,z)\}. \end{equation}

conclusions: $\mathcal{C}_1(TM)$ is invariant under parallel translation and hence a parallel vector subbundle of $TM$

nodes.name: Gradient of the trace lies in the 1-nullity

nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
conclusions: the gradient of $\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$ belongs to the 1-nullity $\mathcal{C}_1(TM)$ everywhere

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 14
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrize Corollary 6, commute third derivatives of $f = \mathrm{tr}\,\kappa$ via curvature, and specialize $y_1=x$, $y_2=y_3=y$.

nodes.name: Symmetrize
nodes.statement:
Let $f := \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$. Since l.h.s. of~\eqref{eq:zweite_vorstufe_zur_Bianchi_identity} is completely symmetric in $u_1,u_2,u_3$, the same is true for the right hand side of that equation. Hence  egin{align*} & 3\,  ig (
abla^3_{y_1,y_2,y_3}f + 2\, \langle y_2,y_3angle \mathrm{d} f(y_1) + \mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2angle \mathrm{d} f(y_3)  ig )\ &\;\;=\;\; \mathfrak{S}_{123}  ig (
abla^3_{y_1,y_2,y_3}f + 2\, \langle y_2,y_3angle \mathrm{d} f(y_1) + \mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2angle \mathrm{d} f(y_3)  ig )\ &\;\;=\;\;\mathfrak{S}_{123} ig (
abla^3_{y_1,y_2,y_3}f + 4\,\langle y_1,y_2angle \mathrm{d} f(y_3) ig )\ &\;\;=\;\;
abla^3_{y_1,y_2,y_3}f + 
abla^3_{y_3,y_1,y_2}f + 
abla^3_{y_2,y_3,y_1}f + 4\,\mathfrak{S}_{123}\,\langle y_1,y_2angle \mathrm{d} f(y_3). \end{align*}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Set $f = \mathrm{tr}\,\kappa$ and symmetrize Corollary 6.

nodes.name: Commute derivatives
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Commute third derivatives of $f$ via curvature.

nodes.name: Collect terms
nodes.statement: Further, \begin{equation*} 6\, \langle y_2,y_3\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_1) + 3\,\mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_3) - 4\,\mathfrak{S}_{123}\,\langle y_1,y_2\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_3)\;\;=\;\;2\, \langle y_2,y_3\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_1) - \mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_3) \end{equation*} We conclude that \begin{align*} & 2\, \langle y_2,y_3\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_1) - \mathfrak{S}_{23}\langle y_1,y_2\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y_3) \;\;=\;\;R_{y_3,y_1} \mathrm{d} f(y_2) + R_{y_2,y_1} \mathrm{d} f(y_3) . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Collect metric terms to an identity with curvature.

nodes.name: Specialize
nodes.statement: Setting $y_1 := x$ and $y_2 := y_3 := y$ we obtain that \begin{equation*} 2\, \mathrm{d} f(R(x,y,y))\;\;=\;\;2\, \langle y,y\rangle \mathrm{d} f(x) - 2\, \langle x,y\rangle \mathrm{d} f(y). \end{equation*} This shows that the gradient of $\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$ belongs to $\mathcal{C}_1(TM)$.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Specializing shows $\mathrm{grad}\,f$ lies in the 1-nullity.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5 (a)
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Show the cyclic sum of $\nabla\kappa$ vanishes on a dense set by cases on $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa$, using holonomy and Berger's classification; then compute $\kappa = \kappa^C$. The key step: non-transitive holonomy forces a locally symmetric space whose 1-nullity is everything.

nodes.name: Hypotheses
nodes.statement: Suppose that~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1}-\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_2} hold for a pair $(\kappa,C)$ and that $\dim(M)\geq 2$.

nodes.statement_short: Assume the system holds and $\dim M \ge 2$.

nodes.name: kappa is Killing
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Show the cyclic sum of $\nabla\kappa$ vanishes, hence $\kappa$ is Killing.

nodes.name: Case: trace locally constant
nodes.statement: We distinguish two cases: If there exists an open neighbourhood around $p$ where $\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$ is constant, then $\kappa$ is Killing on this neighbourhood according to~\eqref{eq:zweite_vorstufe_zur_Bianchi_identity}.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: If $\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa$ is locally constant, Corollary 6 gives Killing.

nodes.name: Case: non-zero trace differential
nodes.statement:
Suppose there exists a point $p\in M$ such that $\mathrm{d} \, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa|_p
eq 0$. In particular, $\kappa$ is not a constant multiple of the metric tensor on any open neighbourhood of $p$. Therefore each neighbourhood of $p$ in $M$ is irreducible according to Lemma~ef{le:M_is_irreducible}. Hence we can assume that $M$ is simply connected and irreducible. Further, recall that the cyclic sum $\mathfrak{S}_{xyz}
abla_x\kappa(y,z)$ is a parallel symmetric 3-tensor according to Lemma~ef{le:Bianchis_cyclic_sum_is_parallel}. Therefore if the holonomy group of $M$ at $p$ acts transitively on the unit sphere of $T_pM$, then the corresponding homogeneous polynomial function $f(x) := 
abla_x\kappa(x,x)$ with $x\in T_pM$ is constant on vectors of equal length. Since the degree of $f$ is odd, we see that $f(x) = f(-x) = - f(x)$ for all $x\in T_pM$ . Therefore $\mathfrak{S}_{xyz} 
abla_x\kappa(y,z)|_p = 0$. If, by contradiction, we assume that the holonomy group acts non-transitively, then $M$ is locally symmetric, $
abla R = 0$, according to Bergers classification of holonomy groups~\cite[5.21]{Ba}. Hence the $1$-nullity~\eqref{eq:curvature_constancy} is a parallel subbundle of $TM$. Since $\mathcal{C}_1(T_pM)
eq \{0\}$ because of Lemma~ef{le:curvature_constancy}, it is non-trivial and thus $\mathcal{C}_1(TM) = TM$ by the irreducibility of $M$. This implies that $M$ has constant sectional curvature, in particular the holonomy group is $\mathrm{SO}(n)$ which acts transitively on the unit sphere of $T_pM$. But this is contrary to our assumptions.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: If $\mathrm{d}\,\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa \neq 0$: irreducible, transitive holonomy kills the odd cubic; non-transitive holonomy contradicts Lemma 14 via Berger.

nodes.name: Density argument
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: The vanishing set is closed and dense, so $\kappa$ is Killing.

nodes.name: kappa equals kappa^C
nodes.statement: We finish the proof of~(a) of Proposition~\ref{p:get_rid} by showing that automatically $\kappa = \kappa^C$: we use~\eqref{eq:Ricci_spur_von_C_1} and~\eqref{eq:vergleich_der_spur_von_kappa_mit_der_skalaren_kruemmung_von_C} to obtain that \begin{align*} \widetilde {\mathrm{Ric}}^C(x,y) \stackrel{\eqref{eq:def_modified_Ricci_trace_und_tilde_scalC}}{=} \mathrm{Ric}^C(x,y) + \frac{1}{4} \nabla^2_{x,y}\mathrm{s}^C \stackrel{\eqref{eq:Ricci_spur_von_C_1},\eqref{eq:vergleich_der_spur_von_kappa_mit_der_skalaren_kruemmung_von_C}}{=} 2 \big (\langle x,y\rangle \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa - \kappa(x,y)\big ). \end{align*} Hence \begin{equation*} \widetilde{\mathrm{s}}^C\;\;=\;\;2(n - 1)\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa. \end{equation*} Inserting the previous into~\eqref{eq:def_kappaC} shows that $\kappa = \kappa^C$. This finishes the proof of Part~(a) of Proposition~\ref{p:get_rid}.
nodes.section: 6 Proof of Theorem~1
nodes.statement_short: Compute $\widetilde{\mathrm{Ric}}^C$ and $\widetilde{s}^C$ to get $\kappa = \kappa^C$.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 5 (b)
nodes.statement:
Let a pair $(\kappa,C)$ with~\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_1}-\eqref{eq:alg_curv_tensor_2} on a compact manifold $M$ with negative definite metric tensor $g$ be given. We claim that $\kappa$ is a constant multiple of $g$: If $M$ is a 1-dimensional sphere, then the space of algebraic curvature tensors is trivial. Hence~\eqref{eq:prolong_2_speziell} and~\eqref{eq:prolong_3_speziell} together show that the third covariant derivative of the pullback $\pi^*\kappa$ of $\kappa$ under the canonical covering $\pi:\mathrm{I\!R}	o M$ vanishes. This implies polynomial growth of $\pi^*\kappa$. But $\pi^*\kappa$ is periodic, hence the previous forces that $\pi^*\kappa$ is constant, i.e. $\kappa$ is trivial. Hence we can assume that $\dim(M)\geq 2$. Using that $\kappa$ is Killing, we conclude from~\eqref{eq:zweite_vorstufe_zur_Bianchi_identity} that $f\;:=\;\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$ satisfies Gallots equation~\eqref{eq:Gallots_Gleichung}. Taking in this equation the trace with respect to $y_1$ and $y_2$, we obtain for the rough Laplacian  egin{equation} 
abla^*
abla \ df \;\;=\;\; (n + 3) \mathrm{d} f. \end{equation} Since on a compact manifold with negative definite metric the rough Laplacian $
abla^*
abla$ is a strictly negative operator, we conclude that $\mathrm{d}\, \mathrm{tr} \, \kappa = 0$, i.e. $\mathrm{tr} \, \kappa$ is a constant $c$. Using~\eqref{eq:Ricci_spur_von_C_1} and~\eqref{eq:Ricci_spur_von_C_2} we thus see that  egin{equation*} 
abla^*
abla  ig (n\, \kappa - c\, g ig )\;\;=\;\;2\, \, (n\, \kappa - c\,g ig ). \end{equation*} Using again the compactness of $M$, we conclude that $\kappa =  rac{c}{n}\, g$. This shows that $\kappa$ is a constant multiple of the metric tensor.

nodes.statement_short: Dimension one by periodicity; otherwise $\mathrm{tr}\,\kappa$ solves Gallot's equation, and negativity of the rough Laplacian on compact $M$ forces $\kappa = cg/n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: For the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:main_2}, it remains to analyze the space of parallel algebraic curvature tensors on the cone over a Riemannian manifold. This is purely a question of holonomy. Gallot showed that the cone over a complete Riemannian manifold is irreducible unless the universal covering of $M$ is isometric to a round sphere. Moreover, the cone $\hat M^{n+1}$ can never be Einstein unless it is Ricci-flat, since the curvature tensor $\hat R$ is purely horizontal according to~\eqref{eq:hat_R_1}. In the following we can assume that $M$ is simply connected and complete. The remaining possible holonomy algebras are according to Bergers classification~\cite[5.21]{Ba}: $\mathfrak{so}(n + 1)$, $\undefined(m)$ or $\mathfrak{su}(m)$ for $n + 1 = 2 m$ and $m \ge 2$, $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$ for $n + 1 = 4 m$ and $m \ge 2$ or $\mathfrak{g}_2$ for $n + 1= 7$ or $\mathfrak{spin}_7$ for $n + 1= 8$. Holonomy algebras $\mathfrak{su}(m)$, $\undefined(m)$ and $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$ of the cone correspond to (Einstein)-Sasakian and 3-Sasakian manifolds, respectively. For a Kähler manifold with Kähler form $\omega$, the Cartan product $\omega\odot\omega$ clearly is a non-trivial parallel algebraic curvature tensor and similar every Hyperkähler manifold with Hyperkähler structure $\{\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3\}$ admits six linearly independent non-trivial parallel algebraic curvature tensors $\omega_i \odot \omega_j$. By the holonomy principle every parallel section of the vector bundle of algebraic curvature tensors on $\hat M$ corresponds to an element of the vector space of algebraic curvature tensors on some tangent space that is fixed by the holonomy algebra. For the proof of Theorem~\ref{th:main_2}, we thus have to show that \begin{itemize} \item the actions of $\mathfrak{g}_2$, $\mathfrak{spin}_7$ and $\mathfrak{so}(n+1)$ on algebraic curvature tensors in dimensions $7$, $8$ and $n+1$ each only have a one-dimensional trivial component, \item the trivial component of $\mathfrak{su}(m)$ and $\undefined(m)$ acting on $\mathcal{C}(\mathrm{I\!R}^{2m})$ is 2-dimensional, \item and the trivial component of $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$ on $\mathcal{C}(\mathrm{I\!R}^{4m})$ is seven-dimensional. \end{itemize} By irreducibility of $\hat M$, every symmetric 2-tensor is a multiple of the metric, i.e. the space of traceless symmetric 2-tensors $\mathrm{Sym}^2(V^*)_0$ remains irreducible over the holonomy algebra. The next two lemmas will show that the space of algebraic curvature tensors $\mathcal{C}(T)$ remains irreducible over $\mathfrak{spin}_7$ or $\lieG2$. This finishes the proof of the classification of Riemannian manifolds matching the statement of Theorem~\ref{th:main_2}.
